name: Alcohol Recovery
tagline: 60 days to break the loop and rewire a sober brain.
description: A neuroscience-based 60-day program to stop drinking — replace the cue→drink→relief loop with healthier rewards, calm the overactive stress response, and build a sober identity.

phases.label: P1
phases.title: Breaking the Cycle
phases.vibe: The first two weeks are about safety and subtraction. Clear alcohol from your space, flood the day with water and sleep, and meet every urge with breath instead of a bottle. You are starving an old habit loop of its cue and its reward.

phases.label: P2
phases.title: Rewiring the Brain
phases.tag: New routine in the same slot.
phases.vibe: Your brain still fires the old craving at the old time — so give it a new routine to run. Where a drink used to go, insert movement, connection, or a ritual. Every repetition thickens the new neural path and thins the old one.

phases.label: P3
phases.title: Building a New Identity
phases.tag: You are a person who doesn't drink.
phases.vibe: This isn't a streak anymore — it's who you are. You protect your sleep, your people, and your purpose. You help someone else and you plan the life sobriety makes possible.

0.title: Morning intention + water
0.note: First thing: 500ml water, then name today's reason to stay sober out loud. Morning cortisol is high — hydration and a stated intention steady the prefrontal cortex before cravings hit.

0.title: Remove one alcohol cue
0.note: Pour out a bottle, hide the glasses, unfollow a bar page. Habits fire from cues — deleting the cue is the cheapest way to weaken the loop.

0.title: HALT check + hydrate
0.note: Ask: am I Hungry, Angry, Lonely, Tired? Most 'cravings' are an unmet basic need. Eat, rest, or reach out instead of drinking.

0.title: 20 min movement
0.note: Walk, run, or lift. Exercise gives you the dopamine and endorphins alcohol used to counterfeit — a clean reward that rebuilds the reward system.

0.title: Urge surfing — SOBER breath
0.note: When the craving comes: Stop, Observe, Breathe, Expand awareness, Respond. Urges peak and pass in ~15-20 min like a wave. Ride it, don't fight it.

0.title: Reach one sober ally
0.note: Text a friend, sponsor, or meeting. Loneliness is a top relapse trigger; connection releases oxytocin, nature's anti-craving.

0.title: Evening journal — 3 wins, 1 trigger
0.note: Write what worked and what tempted you. Naming triggers moves them from the reactive amygdala to the reasoning cortex.

0.title: Lights out — protect sleep
0.note: In bed by a set time, no screens. Alcohol wrecks REM sleep; restoring sleep is the fastest way to cut next-day cravings.

1.title: Morning intention + cold splash
1.note: Water, intention, then 30s cold water on the face. Cold exposure spikes dopamine gently for hours — a natural mood lift to start rewiring the reward baseline.

1.title: Run your replacement ritual
1.note: At your old drinking time, do the swap you chose (tea ritual, walk, gym, call). Same cue, new routine — this is the core of habit rewiring.

1.title: 10 min mindfulness
1.note: Sit and watch the breath. Meditation strengthens the prefrontal cortex's control over impulsive urges and lowers baseline stress.

1.title: 30 min exercise
1.note: Push a little harder than week one. Consistent training re-sensitizes dopamine receptors dulled by alcohol.

1.title: Rehearse one high-risk scenario
1.note: Picture a party or a hard evening and script your exact plan. Mental rehearsal wires the response before you need it.

1.title: Meaningful connection
1.note: A meeting, a call, or coffee with someone sober-supportive. Rebuild the social rewards drinking eroded.

1.title: Gratitude + tomorrow's plan
1.note: List 3 things you're grateful for and plan tomorrow. Gratitude shifts the brain toward the reward you already have.

2.title: Sober morning ritual
2.note: Water, movement, intention — automatic now. A stable morning is the anchor of a stable identity.

2.title: 30-45 min toward a goal
2.note: Study, build, create — pour the freed-up energy into something that matters. Purpose is the long-term replacement for the bottle.

2.title: Train — your standard now
2.note: Movement is who you are, not a chore. It keeps the reward system healthy for good.

2.title: Support someone else
2.note: Share your experience or check on someone struggling. Helping others is one of the strongest protectors against relapse.

2.title: 10-15 min mindfulness
2.note: Keep the prefrontal cortex strong. Calm brains don't need to escape.

2.title: Identity journal
2.note: Write as the person you've become: 'I am someone who...'. Repeated self-statements reshape self-concept.

2.title: Protect sleep
2.note: Guard your recovery's foundation. Consistent sleep locks in every gain.

quotes: The urge is a wave. You are the surfer, not the ocean.
You never regret the drink you didn't take.
Sobriety is not deprivation — it's the return of everything alcohol stole.
One day at a time is still forward.
Your brain is healing every single sober hour.
Cravings lie. They promise relief and deliver the trap.
The opposite of addiction is connection.
You are not missing out. You are getting yourself back.
Discomfort now, or the same regret forever. Choose the growth.
Two months sober rewires what two years of promises never could.
